newsitem.title: ESTONIA: ESTONIA-HANSA UNSURE ON PROFIT FORECAST CHANGE.
newsitem.headline: ESTONIA-HANSA UNSURE ON PROFIT FORECAST CHANGE.

text.p: Hansapank said on Monday its first quarter consolidated results were better than expected but did not know yet if it would revise its profit estimate.
"The results were pretty good and somewhat better than we expected," Rain Lohmus, Hansapank vice chairman, told Reuters.
The bank's board will in the coming weeks discuss the group's results and also a possible revision of its profit estimate, Lohmus said.
"It is not clear if we want to change our estimate," he added. The bank is expecting a group net profit this year of 320 million kroons.
"Hansapank has always been conservative and the last two years have shown it has always been better than estimates," Lohmus said.
Hansapank earlier said its first quarter group net profit was 136.1 million kroons.
The figure included the sale of 350,000 shares in Hoiupank in January, on which Hansapank earned over 30 million kroons.
Lohmus said that its subsidiaries had good results in the first quarter and it did not expect its Latvian subsidiary Hansabank-Latvija to make a profit, Lohmus added.
"The expenses were less than expected...and the earnings were good," he added.
